title: Paediatric cardiac arrest (PALS)
subject: paediatrics
summary: High-quality CPR (15:2 with two rescuers), adrenaline 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (max 1 mg) every 3 to 5 minutes and early for non-shockable rhythms, shocks of 2 J/kg then 4 J/kg (max 10 J/kg or adult dose), and amiodarone 5 mg/kg or lidocaine 1 mg/kg for refractory VF or pulseless VT (AHA/AAP 2025).

sections.title: Recognise arrest
items: Unresponsive, not breathing normally (or only gasping) and no definite pulse within 10 seconds: start CPR. Also start compressions if heart rate is below 60/min with poor perfusion despite oxygenation and ventilation.

Most paediatric arrests are hypoxic or asphyxial (respiratory failure or shock). Shockable rhythms are less common; suspect them in sudden witnessed collapse, heart disease, electrocution or drug toxicity.
Applies to infants and children up to 18 years, excluding newborns at birth (use the neonatal resuscitation protocol).

sections.title: High-quality CPR
items: Compress at 100 to 120/min to at least one-third of the chest depth (about 4 cm in infants, about 5 cm in children, 5 to 6 cm in adolescents), allow full recoil and keep pauses under 10 seconds.

Ratio 30:2 for a single rescuer; 15:2 with two or more rescuers until puberty, 30:2 after puberty. With an advanced airway, compress continuously and give 1 breath every 2 to 3 seconds (20 to 30/min), adjusted for age.
Infants: 2-thumb encircling-hands technique; if the chest cannot be encircled, use the heel of one hand. The 2-finger technique is no longer recommended.
Ventilate with 100% oxygen by bag and mask; intubation must not interrupt compressions. Prefer a cuffed tube and confirm placement with waveform capnography.
Obtain IV or IO access early (go straight to IO if IV is not quick), attach a monitor-defibrillator and change compressors every 2 minutes.

sections.title: Non-shockable rhythm (asystole, PEA)
items: Give adrenaline 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (0.1 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL, max 1 mg) as early as possible, within 5 minutes of starting compressions, then every 3 to 5 minutes.
Continue CPR in 2-minute cycles with rhythm checks; switch to the shockable pathway if VF or pulseless VT appears.
Look for and treat reversible causes: hypoxia, hypovolaemia, hydrogen ion (acidosis), hypo- or hyperkalaemia, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins and thrombosis.

sections.title: Shockable rhythm (VF, pulseless VT)
items: Shock at 2 J/kg as soon as possible and resume CPR immediately for 2 minutes; second shock 4 J/kg; later shocks 4 J/kg or more, up to a maximum of 10 J/kg or the adult dose.
Give adrenaline 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (max 1 mg) after the second shock, then every 3 to 5 minutes.
Shock-refractory VF or pulseless VT: amiodarone 5 mg/kg IV/IO bolus (max 300 mg), repeatable up to a total of 15 mg/kg, or lidocaine 1 mg/kg IV/IO.

Use a manual defibrillator with paediatric pads where available; otherwise an AED with a paediatric attenuator, or a standard AED if nothing else is available. Place pads front and back in small children so they do not touch.

sections.title: Monitoring during CPR
items: Use waveform capnography to monitor CPR quality and detect return of circulation; do not use any single ETCO2 value alone to stop resuscitation.
If an arterial line is in place, aim for diastolic pressure of at least 25 mmHg in infants and at least 30 mmHg in children aged 1 year or more.

Check glucose, potassium, ionised calcium and a blood gas when access allows. Routine sodium bicarbonate or calcium is not recommended; give them for specific indications such as hyperkalaemia or sodium channel blocker toxicity.

sections.title: After return of spontaneous circulation
items: Target SpO2 94 to 99% and normal PaCO2 (35 to 45 mmHg); avoid both hypoxaemia and hyperoxia.
Keep systolic and mean blood pressure above the 10th centile for age with fluids and vasoactive drugs. Treat seizures and use continuous EEG in comatose children where available.

Comatose children: monitor core temperature continuously and prevent fever above 37.5 °C. Targeted temperature management for up to 5 days is reasonable, either 32 to 34 °C then 36 to 37.5 °C, or 36 to 37.5 °C throughout.
Transfer to a PICU. Where available, consider extracorporeal CPR early for refractory in-hospital arrest from a cardiac cause.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Long pauses for intubation, line insertion or rhythm checks: keep hands-off time under 10 seconds.
Delaying adrenaline in asystole or PEA; aim to give the first dose within 5 minutes of starting compressions.
Dosing errors: 1 mg/mL (1:1000) adrenaline must be diluted to 0.1 mg/mL for IV use; use a weight chart or length-based tape and a second-person check.
Over-ventilation after an advanced airway reduces venous return and coronary perfusion.

drugs.name: Adrenaline (epinephrine) 0.1 mg/mL
drugs.dose: 0.01 mg/kg (0.1 mL/kg) IV/IO every 3 to 5 minutes, max 1 mg per dose
drugs.notes: Endotracheal 0.1 mg/kg (0.1 mL/kg of 1 mg/mL) only if no IV/IO access.

drugs.name: Amiodarone
drugs.dose: 5 mg/kg IV/IO bolus (max 300 mg), may repeat to a total of 15 mg/kg

drugs.name: Lidocaine
drugs.notes: Alternative to amiodarone for shock-refractory VF or pulseless VT.

drugs.name: Defibrillation energy
drugs.dose: 2 J/kg first shock, 4 J/kg second shock, then 4 J/kg or more (max 10 J/kg or adult dose)
